text:
sam: heads up — noticed a ~10% P95 regression on dedicated perf runs after the recent kernel-selector tweak. perfetto trace shows a burst of queue_time spikes and a bunch of tiny matmul launches around the same window :eyes:

maria: can you post the perfetto nsys links and the exact run config? suspect kernel affinity or a fallback to slower matmul path.

sam: perfetto: https://perfetto.google.cn/trace/ABCDEFG (private)
nsys snippet i pulled out:
```
GPU queue_time: 4.2ms -> 22.7ms (spike)
kernels:
  matmul_fast x 48 (avg 0.18ms)
  matmul_dispatch x 310 (avg 0.02ms)
kernel-launch jitter: ~200us gaps between small kernels
```
config: `batch_window_ms=6, batch_max_tokens=2048, kv_sweep_interval_s=300, kernel_selector=v2`

oliver: fwiw i saw similar pattern when kvcache sweep runs aligned with batch window — sweep does a bunch of CPU callbacks that serialize launch. do you have logs around kvcache.sweep?

sam: attaching log snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] kvcache: sweep started (hot=12, cold=34)
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] batching: window open (slot=17)
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] kernel_selector: chose matmul_dispatch (reason=small_batch)
[2026-03-10T14:12:03Z] gpu: queue_time=21.7ms
```

jen: @sam can you repro with `kv_sweep_interval_s=0` (disable periodic sweep) and/or bump `batch_window_ms` to 10? quick A/B will tell if sweep alignment is culprit. also try forcing `kernel_selector=legacy` to see if the new selector introduced the regression.

maria: i'll run two microbenchmarks in CI with these flags. command i use to capture a tight kernel timeline:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/nsys --trace=cuda,cudnn,osrt --sample=none --stats=true --capture-range=cudaLaunch -- ./bench_runner --num-requests=2000
```
add `--collect-stack` if you want host-side call stacks.

perfbot: perf regression alert: commit 8c9d1b2 changed kernel_selector logic (PR #4257). Regression window matches traces reported by @sam. See CI diff: https://git.internal/pr/4257 

oliver: quick hypothesis: new selector favors splitting large ops into many small dispatches on quantized paths; when kvcache sweep/GC runs it adds CPU stalls just before kernel launches -> increase in queue_time for that batch which in turn makes scheduler open many small kernel launches (cycle).

sam: that matches what i'm seeing. maria — can you capture a run where i flip `kvcache.sweep_threshold=0.9` (delay sweep) and `batch_window_ms=12`? also try `--kernel-hint=prefer_fast_matmul` to force the matmul_fast path.

maria: on it. will push results in ~25m.

jen: long-term we should make kvcache sweeps aware of batching windows (avoid starting sweep during active windows) or have sweeps yield more cooperatively. simple guard: don't run sweep if `batch_open=true` and last_launch < 5ms.

oliver: +1. could also add a kernel_selector penalty when recent queue_time > threshold to avoid micro-launch storms.

sam: thanks team. if anyone else wants to repro locally: small repro script i used:
```
# repro script
for i in 1 2 3; do
  ./bench_runner --concurrency=16 --batch-window-ms=6 --kernel-selector=v2 --kv-sweep-interval=300
  sleep 5
done
```

maria: results: disabling sweep removed the P95 regression (P95 back to baseline), bumping window to 12ms reduced spike severity ~60%, forcing legacy selector avoids the tiny-launch pattern. i uploaded raw nsys captures to the perf bucket.

sam: great find — looks like an interaction bug between selector and kvcache sweep. filing a bug and tagging PR that introduced heuristics.

perfbot: created issue PERF-2146: "kernel-selector v2 + kvcache sweep -> queue_time spike & mini-kernel storms" (assigned to @maria and @oliver).

jen: for the immediate mitigation let's revert selector default in the next canary and add the sweep-guard patch. i'll open a revert + mitigation PR. :thumbsup:

sam: awesome. follow-ups: add an automated microbenchmark that runs with aligned/unaligned sweep timing so we don't regress this again.

oliver: noted — i'll add it to perf-tests/benchmarks.

sam: thanks all :) :rocket:
